feedback: Approved for the race. Judged from earlier races and the candidate's own contents only. This candidate has not raced, so it states no outcome. It is valid: sensors at x = ±0.08 are on the contract maximum, which is allowed, and every other field is inside range. It changes one group, the outer sensor geometry, from the best raced design (iteration 6, 64.7409). Iteration 9 showed that line_loss search_right changes nothing (64.7408 against 64.7409, identical per-track metrics), so the line-loss direction is not a lever and should stay as it is. Slalom progress has sat at 0.1025 across iterations 3 to 6 and 9 whatever the gain or sensor size, which points to reach. Iteration 6 showed that moving the outer sensors from ±0.04 to ±0.06 lifted s-bend progress from 0.04 to 0.14. Two cautions: at the edge of the allowed range, the outer weights act on the tape earlier and may raise steering_oscillation further (it was 0.159 on the oval and 0.173 on the s-bend at iteration 6), and the oval may lose some progress, as it did at ±0.06 with sensor_size 0.016. With two iterations left, racing this change is worth more than another paper revision. Reading the race: (a) If slalom progress rises above about 0.10 and line_loss_events fall toward 0 while the s-bend holds near 0.14, keep ±0.08 for the final design. (b) If the s-bend or oval falls below iteration 6 levels, the spread has passed its useful range, so return to ±0.06 and take slalom reach through base_speed or sensor forward position (y). (c) If the robot tracks without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6 in a single-group revision. Report progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, plus completion_time and rms_error.
requested_changes: If slalom progress rises above 0.10 with line_loss_events near 0 and s-bend near 0.14 (iteration 6 baseline), keep sensor x = ±0.08 and carry it into the final design; iteration 6 showed the ±0.04 to ±0.06 step lifted s-bend progress from 0.04 to 0.14.

If the s-bend or oval falls below the iteration 6 levels (s-bend 0.14, oval 0.22), return the outer sensors to x = ±0.06, since the wider spread costs more than it gains, and address slalom through base_speed or sensor y position.
If the robot tracks without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, set base_speed = 1.6 in a single-group revision, because the 3.0 s limit needs an average speed of about 1.5 m/s.
